title: Fix #8: Scope selectors for multiple comment forms
body:
# Description

Fix multiple-comment-form initialization so every comma-separated selector is scoped to its post container.

Previously only the first selector received the container prefix. For example, `#commentform,.comment-form` became `#post-one #commentform,.comment-form`, leaving `.comment-form` global. Every delegated handler therefore matched later forms, and submitting the second form could run the first post container's update path.

This change scopes each selector component independently, includes comment links in the same scoping, and rebuilds both frontend bundles.

Fixes #8

## Type of PR

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Security fix
- [ ] Other (please describe)

### Where is the Bug?

- [x] Comment posting

- [ ] Error messages and Overlay
- [x] JavaScript file
- [ ] Other

# How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Browser tests
- [ ] Performance tests
- [x] Local testing

A two-post browser reproduction loaded the production bundle with duplicate WordPress comment form IDs/classes. Before the fix, submitting post two selected post one's comments/form/respond containers. After the fix, sequential submissions produced requests for posts 1 and 2 and selected their respective scoped containers.

title: Fix translated comment submission messages
body:
# Description

Fix comment-status messages and other plugin strings so they can follow the active WordPress locale.

- Rename bundled PO/MO catalogs to WordPress's `wp-ajaxify-comments-{locale}` convention, correct the Vietnamese locale to `vi`, and normalize the language-directory path.
- Recompile all bundled MO files from their PO sources and keep them as temporary fallbacks until community replacements are available.
- Keep untouched label defaults in canonical English storage, translate them at runtime, and preserve genuinely customized labels.
- Register translations for admin scripts, correct stray JavaScript text domains, and rebuild the affected bundles.
- Regenerate the source POT, add language directory metadata, and update translator guidance.

Fixes #13

## WordPress.org translation audit

The WordPress.org translation project exists and currently contains 500 stable originals. The 18 bundled locales all show 0% approved stable translations, and no language packs have been generated.

Comparing the bundled catalogs with the current 492-entry source POT found 134 exact translated entries plus 450 fuzzy candidates. Issue #17 tracks importing those translations into GlotPress, obtaining locale-editor review, and removing each bundled fallback only after WordPress.org distributes its replacement pack.

## Type of PR

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Security fix
- [ ] Other (please describe)

- [ ] Lazy loading
- [x] Error messages and Overlay

- [x] Other: translation catalog discovery and locale-aware saved defaults

- `npm run build` completed successfully; the unavailable, unused `@sweetalert2/theme-wordpress-admin` package was omitted only from the local install, and the committed manifests remain unchanged.
- PHP syntax checks passed for all changed PHP and generated asset files.
- `msgfmt --check` passed for all 18 bundled PO catalogs (legacy header warnings only).
- Every MO catalog was decompiled and compared successfully with the non-fuzzy translated entries in its PO source.
- All bundled filenames now match the plugin text domain and WordPress locale, including Vietnamese `vi`.
- The five comment-submission status/error message IDs are translated in every bundled catalog.
- POT regeneration produced the same 492 source message IDs.
- Focused option-label checks confirmed canonical storage, runtime translation, historical defaults, and custom-label preservation.
- ESLint still reports 55 pre-existing errors in the touched source files; none are on changed lines.
